arxiv-2005-01351.title: Anchors Based Method for Fingertips Position Estimation from a Monocular RGB Image using Deep Neural Network
arxiv-2005-01351.creator: Purnendu Mishra, and Kishor Sarawadekar
arxiv-2005-01351.description: Abstract In Virtual, augmented, and mixed reality, the use of hand gestures is increasingly becoming popular to reduce the difference between the virtual and real world. The precise location of the fingertip is essential/crucial for a seamless experience. Much of the research work is based on using depth information for the estimation of the fingertips position.

arxiv-2102-03979.title: Prospects for Constraining Interacting Dark Energy Models with 21 cm Intensity Mapping Experiments
arxiv-2102-03979.creator: Ming Zhang, Bo Wang, Peng-Ju Wu, Jing-Zhao Qi, Yidong Xu, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
arxiv-2102-03979.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ming Zhang, Bo Wang, Peng-Ju Wu, Jing-Zhao Qi, Yidong Xu, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang. We forecast constraints on cosmological parameters in the interacting dark energy models using the mock data generated for neutral hydrogen intensity mapping (IM) experiments. In this work, we only consider the interacting dark energy models with energy transfer rate Q = β ​ H ​ ρ c Q=\beta H\rho_{\rm c} , and take BINGO, FAST, SKA1-MID, and Tianlai as typical examples of the 21 cm IM experiments.

arxiv-2108-02949.title: Auxiliary Class Based Multiple Choice Learning
arxiv-2108-02949.creator: Sihwan Kim, Dae Yon Jung, Taejang Park
arxiv-2108-02949.description: Abstract The merit of ensemble learning lies in having different outputs from many individual models on a single input, i . e . i.e. , the diversity of the base models. The high quality of diversity can be achieved when each model is specialized to different subsets of the whole dataset.

arxiv-2210-16632.title: Certifying randomness in quantum state collapse
arxiv-2210-16632.creator: Liang-Liang Sun, Xingjian Zhang, Xiang-Zhou, Zheng-Da Li, Xiongfeng Ma, Jingyun Fan, Sixia Yu
arxiv-2210-16632.description: Abstract The unpredictable process of state collapse caused by quantum measurements makes the generation of quantum randomness possible. In this paper, we explore the quantitative connection between the randomness generation and the state collapse and provide a randomness verification protocol under the assumptions: (I) independence between the source and the measurement devices and (II) the Lüders’ rule for collapsing state.

arxiv-2305-17966.title: Quafu-RL: The Cloud Quantum Computers based Quantum Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-17966.creator: BAQIS Quafu Group
arxiv-2305-17966.description: Abstract With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, hybrid quantum-classical machine learning has shown numerous potential applications at the current stage, with expectations of being achievable in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. Quantum reinforcement learning, as an indispensable study, has recently demonstrated its ability to solve standard benchmark environments with formally provable theoretical advantages over classical counterparts.

arxiv-2408-06261.title: Open-Source Molecular Processing Pipeline for Generating Molecules
arxiv-2408-06261.creator: V Shreyas, Jose Siguenza, Karan Bania, Bharath Ramsundar
arxiv-2408-06261.description: Abstract Generative models for molecules have shown considerable promise for use in computational chemistry, but remain difficult to use for non-experts. For this reason, we introduce open-source infrastructure for easily building generative molecular models into the widely used DeepChem [ 25 ] library with the aim of creating a robust and reusable molecular generation pipeline.

arxiv-2409-13851.title: Learning Ordering in Crystalline Materials with Symmetry-Aware Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2409-13851.creator: Jiayu Peng, James Damewood, Jessica Karaguesian, Jaclyn R, Lunger, Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli, Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Center for Computational Science and Engineering,Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139, USA, Equal contribution; rafagb@mit.edu (R.G.-B.)

arxiv-2410-21210.title: Mode Stability of Hermitian Instantons
arxiv-2410-21210.creator: Lars ANDERSSON a, Bernardo ARANEDA b and Mattias DAHL c
arxiv-2410-21210.description: Abstract In this note, we prove the Riemannian analog of black hole mode stability for Hermitian, non-self-dual gravitational instantons which are either asymptotically locally flat (ALF) and Ricci-flat, or compact and Einstein with positive cosmological constant. We show that the Teukolsky equation on any such manifold is a positive definite operator.

arxiv-2505-22973.title: EquiReg: Equivariance Regularized Diffusion for Inverse Problems
arxiv-2505-22973.creator: Bahareh Tolooshams btolooshams@ualberta.ca, Aditi Chandrashekar * ajc10180@nyu.edu, Rayhan Zirvi * rayhanzirvi@caltech.edu, Abbas Mammadov abbas.mammadov@reuben.ox.ac.uk, Jiachen Yao jiachen@caltech.edu, Chuwei Wang chuweiw@caltech.edu, Anima Anandkumar anima@caltech.edu
arxiv-2505-22973.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bahareh Tolooshams btolooshams@ualberta.ca, Aditi Chandrashekar * ajc10180@nyu.edu, Rayhan Zirvi * rayhanzirvi@caltech.edu, Abbas Mammadov abbas.mammadov@reuben.ox.ac.uk, Jiachen Yao jiachen@caltech.edu, Chuwei Wang chuweiw@caltech.edu, Anima Anandkumar anima@caltech.edu. Diffusion models represent the state-of-the-art for solving inverse problems such as image restoration tasks. Diffusion-based inverse solvers incorporate a likelihood term to guide prior sampling, generating data consistent with the posterior distribution. However, due to the intractability of the likelihood, most methods rely on isotropic Gaussian approximations, which can push estimates off the data manifold and produce inconsistent, poor reconstructions.

arxiv-2602-23149.title: Interface for variants of the contact process
arxiv-2602-23149.creator: Isabella Alvarenga, Daniel Valesin
arxiv-2602-23149.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Isabella Alvarenga, Daniel Valesin. pmc-10654174.title: Prevalence of anatomical variations at the suboccipital (V3) segment of the vertebral artery: a systematic review
pmc-10654174.creator: Bukola R. Omotoso, Rohen Harrichandparsad, Lelika Lazarus

pmc-11615514.description: BackgroundInflammation is one of the hallmarks of cancer and is associated with tumor growth. Tumor endothelial cells (TECs) demonstrate inflamed phenotypes. Endothelial inflammation initiates thrombus formation, which is the second cause of cancer‐related deaths. Epigallocatechin‐3‐O‐gallate (EGCG), a natural compound in green tea, has demonstrated an anti‐inflammatory effect.

pmc-11681869.title: Enhanced solar light photocatalytic degradation of tetracycline by aero-GaN and ZnO microtetrapods functionalized with noble metal nanodots

pmc-11904412.title: Antidrug antibodies to adalimumab do not associate with immunologically related adverse events
pmc-11904412.creator: Sophie Tourdot, Maria-Dolores Vazquez-Abad, Donna S. Cox, Chun-Hua Cai, Karen Wang, Wuyan Zhang, Christopher Lepsy
pmc-11904412.description: IntroductionUnwanted immune responses (UIRs) to biologics can negatively impact treatment efficacy and pharmacokinetics and/or induce adverse events (AEs). We characterized the UIR profile of adalimumab (ADL) using data from a phase 3, randomized, interchangeability study of reference ADL (ADL-REF; Humira®) and ADL biosimilar PF-06410293 in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

pmc-12488896.title: Candidate serum metabolite biomarkers of subclinical Haemonchus contortus infection in sheep
pmc-12488896.creator: Hamza Jawad, Desiree Gellatly, Yaogeng Lei, Sean Thompson, Shima Borzouie, Olufemi Osonowo, John S Gilleard, Younes Miar, Seyed Ali Goldansaz, Ghader Manafiazar

The gold standard, fecal egg count, identifies only clinical stages after egg count establishment and shedding in the feces. However, detection at the sub-clinical phase could offer a critical window for strategic deworming and prevent production losses.

pmc-12511358.title: Association between toothbrushing habits and hypertension in the general population
pmc-12511358.creator: Ayano Tezuka, Takuro Kubozono, Takeko Kawabata, Shin Kawasoe, Satoko Ojima, Satoshi Yamaguchi, Yuichi Akasaki, Koji Higuchi, So Kuwahata, Toshihiro Takenaka, Keitaro Nishi, Maya Nakamura, Tatsuo Okui, Mitsuru Ohishi
pmc-12511358.description: Periodontitis has been linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD), suggesting that oral care may play a role in CVD prevention. In contrast, hypertension has been linked to oral health; however, its association with toothbrushing habits is unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the relationship between toothbrushing habits and hypertension.

pmc-12590656.title: Establishment of rabbit models of lumbar disc degeneration using three methods monitored via X-ray: a comparative study
pmc-12590656.creator: Xuewen Shi, Yunfei Li, Jinpeng Lou, Huijuan An, Tong Wu, Yinwen Zheng, Wenji Wang, Tao Zhang, Hua Liu
pmc-12590656.description: BackgroundIntervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is a major cause of chronic lower back pain and associated spinal disorders. Animal models play a crucial role in elucidating the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying IDD and in the development of potential treatments. Various techniques have been used to induce IDD, including annulus fibrosus puncture, nucleus pulposus aspiration (NPA), and chemical injections.

pmc-12640083.title: PickMe: Sample Selection for Species Tree Reconstruction using Coalescent Weighted Quartets
pmc-12640083.creator: Joseph Rusinko, Yu Cai, Allison Crysler, Katherine Thompson, Julien Boutte, Mark Fishbein, Shannon C K Straub
pmc-12640083.description: After collecting large datasets for phylogenomics studies, researchers must decide which genes or samples to include when reconstructing a species tree. pmc-12731251.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Nanosensor Platforms for Non-Invasive Breathomic Diagnostics
pmc-12731251.creator: Vishal Chaudhary, Pradeep Bhadola
pmc-12731251.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Global healthcare settings are increasingly burdened by critical diseases, where conventional diagnostics are often expensive, invasive, time-consuming and centralised. It creates a critical gap for rapid, accessible, portable and non-invasive health assessment. AI-powered Nanosensors for Breathomics Diagnostics (AND) platforms have emerged as a transformative solution to this complex global problem, integrating highly sensitive nanomaterials with advanced machine intelligence to detect disease biomarkers in exhaled breath.
